summary.headline: Som Distilleries H1 FY27 PAT fell to Rs 1.7 crore from Rs 61.56 crore as mobile plant outage cut volumes 39%.
summary.overview: Operations at the Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal) mobile facility were restored and production and dispatches have restarted after roughly eight to nine months of suspension. H1 FY27 consolidated total income fell about 43% to Rs 454.7 crore, and total volume fell about 39% to 77.47 lakh cases. Q2 alone posted 31.6 lakh cases, total income of Rs 185.9 crore, EBITDA of Rs 17.7 crore and PAT of Rs 0.14 crore. Management guided FY27 turnover of about Rs 1,000 crore with EBITDA margin near 10%, and expects to recover Madhya Pradesh market share in three to six months.

segments.name: Madhya Pradesh (Bhopal mobile facility)
segments.commentary: Licence restored and production and dispatches recommenced after about eight to nine months of suspension. Management expects to regain its 45%+ market share in three to six months, reaching it around February.

segments.name: Uttar Pradesh brewery
segments.commentary: Production began around June; it has placed product in about one-third of the market and close to 2,000 outlets. Management says EBITDA breakeven is expected at 20-25% capacity utilisation, targeted by Q2 FY28.

segments.name: Core markets (Karnataka, Odisha, Tamil Nadu)
segments.commentary: Odisha, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu contributed most of the volume in Q2 and H1. Tamil Nadu market share reached about 4% against a 5-6% target over one to two years.

segments.name: IMFL (Mahaaaa whisky brand, mid-premium)
segments.commentary: IMFL was about 14-15% of revenue last year; the target is 15-20% of revenue in the short to medium term. The Mahavat whisky launch, paused by the shutdown, is being revisited over the next two to three months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 turnover guidance of about Rs 1,000 crore with EBITDA margin around 10% (H1 consolidated EBITDA margin 7%).
H2 FY27 consolidated net revenue expected at about Rs 550 crore (as stated on the call).
Management expects Madhya Pradesh volumes to recover to prior-year levels within two quarters.
Bhopal utilisation and realisation guidance deferred to the Q3 call because of the lean season.
IMFL expected to reach 15-20% of revenue in the short to medium term (next year per management).
capex_capacity: Installed capacity is 48.2 million cases of beer and 5.1 million cases of IMFL across Bhopal, Hafen and Odisha facilities, plus the new Uttar Pradesh brewery.
UP phase two has sanctioned bank letters of about Rs 210 crore; timing and debt/equity mix to be decided within the next five to six months.
Plan to convert the Odisha and UP plants into wholly owned subsidiaries is in the works; no timeline given.
Woodpecker Green Agri-Nutrient is now 100% owned by the listed entity (earlier 26%).
demand_pricing: Management says can prices rose but have stabilised; glass bottle prices rose in Q1 and have since stabilised.
Realisation per case fell year on year, which management attributed to the loss of Madhya Pradesh volume, a large share of which was canned (higher realisation).
Odisha capacity is about 35% of industry demand in that state. A Carlsberg India contract-bottling deal was renewed for three years; management declined to quantify margin.
Management reports a repeat-order rate it describes as encouraging for the new IMFL brand, which was placed in 1,500-2,000 outlets before the licence issue.

qa_highlights.question: Has market share been lost in Madhya Pradesh, and can numbers return within two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to regain over 45% share in three to six months, around February. Recovery is in an off-season, so it targets growth on a year-on-year basis over three to six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP phase two capex, funding and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 210 crore of bank sanction is in place. Timing and debt versus equity will be decided within the next six months.

qa_highlights.question: Was all Bhopal loss booked in Q2, and is there any write-off on the Rs 25 crore finished stock?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said all losses have been booked. No write-offs have been taken and no stock has expired.

qa_highlights.question: What is the UP breakeven and margin recovery timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: UP EBITDA breakeven is expected at 20-25% utilisation, by Q2 FY28. Group EBITDA margin is expected to end FY27 around 10%, from 7% in H1.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the Carlsberg contract bottling renewed rather than using lines for own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Odisha capacity equals about 35% of state industry demand, so tying up with a brand with substantial volume improves utilisation. Margin comparison was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Will the annual licence renewal for the Bhopal plant (due March 2027) be smooth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the renewal should be a regular process, as it has been for 30 years. Management is not pursuing compensatory claims against the government.

risks_watch: Recovery of Madhya Pradesh volume and 45%+ share is unproven and falls in the off-season; management's three-to-six-month timeline is untested.
FY27 guidance (Rs 1,000 crore turnover, 10% EBITDA margin) implies a sharp H2 step-up from H1 turnover of about Rs 455 crore and a 7% H1 margin.
Gross debt rose by Rs 100 crore in Q2 and gross debt/equity reached 0.44 from 0.30, with UP phase two capex still to be funded.
Regulatory exposure: the Bhopal licence was suspended for about nine months; the annual renewal is due in March 2027, and no insurance cover is in place.
Management declined to disclose Carlsberg contract margins, the Odisha licence economics, and Bhopal utilisation; the next call is expected to give more on these.
summary.management_tone: Management was cautious and somewhat evasive. It acknowledged the shortfall as "clearly below our expectations" and gave firm targets for volume recovery and FY27 guidance. Several answers were vague or deferred, including on Bhopal utilisation, margins and the IMFL metrics.
key_quotes: These numbers are clearly below our expectations.
We believe it is important to be transparent about the extent of the impact and the factors that led to it.
The most important development is that operations at our mobile facility have been restored and production and dispatches have been recommenced.

growth.why: FY27 turnover guided at about Rs 1,000 crore (held) with EBITDA margin near 10%, and H2 consolidated net revenue about Rs 550 crore, but H1 income fell ~43% and volume ~39%, with Madhya Pradesh recovery in 3-6 months and UP phase-two capex deferred about six months, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management hopes to end FY27 at around 10% EBITDA margin versus 7.24% in H1 FY27, and the UP brewery targets EBITDA breakeven at 20-25% utilisation by Q2 FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: UP brewery began production around June 2026 and is targeted to reach EBITDA breakeven at 20-25% utilisation by Q2 FY28; UP phase two (about Rs 210 crore bank sanction) is deferred, so no new capacity is confirmed inside the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 volume fell about 39% to 77.47 lakh cases, but management expects Madhya Pradesh to regain its 45%+ share in three to six months and H2 consolidated net revenue of about Rs 550 crore versus H1 of Rs 454.7 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Installed capacity of 48.2 million cases beer is under-used after the Bhopal outage and the company says its immediate priority is utilisation; UP phase two sanctioned at about Rs 210 crore with timing and debt/equity mix to be decided within 5-6 months.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 turnover guidance of about Rs 1,000 crore was only held, and H1 turnover of about Rs 455 crore implies H2 needs about Rs 550 crore, a sharp step-up that is unproven.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 guidance of Rs 1,000 crore and 10% EBITDA margin needs H2 revenue of about Rs 550 crore versus H1 Rs 455 crore; Bhopal recovery is in off-season and the Rs 1,000 crore figure sits on an untested 3-6 month share recovery.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: The Mahavat whisky launch, paused by the shutdown, is being revisited over the next two to three months, and IMFL target is 15-20% of revenue versus 14-15% last year, with repeat orders described as encouraging.

rows.label: Madhya Pradesh licence restored and volume recovery to 45%+ share
rows.why: Bhopal licence restored after about 8-9 months of suspension; management expects 45%+ share in 3-6 months, but the recovery is unproven and falls in the off-season.

rows.label: Odisha Carlsberg contract bottling renewed for three years
rows.why: Renewed for three years to improve utilisation of Odisha capacity, which is about 35% of Odisha industry demand; margin not disclosed.

rows.label: Bhopal annual licence renewal due March 2027
rows.why: Management says renewal should be a regular process as it has been for 30 years, but no insurance cover is in place after a 8-9 month suspension.

tone.note: Management was cautious and partly evasive, calling the shortfall clearly below expectations and deferring Bhopal utilisation, margin and IMFL metrics to the Q3 call; analysts pressed on MP share recovery, UP capex funding and the step-up needed in H2.

oneOffs.what: Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh) mobile plant suspended about 8-9 months, cutting H1 volume ~39% YoY; this is a disruption depressing growth, not a repeating feature
No base-period gain identified in the brief; year-ago H1 FY26 PAT of Rs 61.56 crore was the normal business, so no base gain is claimed

quality.why: H1 FY27 total volume fell about 39% YoY to 77.47 lakh cases and total income fell about 43% to Rs 454.7 crore, driven almost entirely by the eight-to-nine-month suspension of the Bhopal plant, so the decline is a disruption rather than the recurring business, and realisation per case also fell because the lost volume was higher-realisation canned product.
